```{r}
#| include: false

options(CausalStructures.auto_install = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(CausalStructures)
setup()
```

`plot()` draws a `cgraph` with grid graphics. We `plot` deliberately impose no
conventions on how to draw causal graphs, such as making bidirected edges
(`<->`) an arc. Instead, we just provide the capabilties, and downstream
packages are encouraged to build an opinionated layer on top.

## Basic usage

Pass any `cgraph` to `plot()`.Every edge mark is supported natively:

```{r}
#| label: edge-marks

unknown <- cgraph(A %<->% B %o->% C %o-o% A, class = "UNKNOWN")
plot(unknown)
```

## Layouts

`layout` controls node placement and defaults to `"stress"`.

```{r}
#| label: layout-spring

dag <- cgraph(
  C %-->% X,
  A %-->% X + K,
  X %-->% F + D,
  K %-->% Y,
  D %-->% Y + G,
  Y %-->% H
)
plot(dag, layout = "spring")
```

`layout` can be:

  | `layout`       | Algorithm                           |
  | -------------- | ----------------------------------- |
  | `"spring"`     | Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed |
  | `"stress"`     | Stress majorization (the default)   |
  | `"sfdp"`       | Scalable Force-Directed Placement   |
  | `"spectral"`   | Spectral layout                     |
  | `"shell"`      | Concentric shells                   |
  | `"squaregrid"` | Square grid                         |

All come from
[NetworkLayout.jl](https://github.com/JuliaGraphs/NetworkLayout.jl); see
`?cgraph_layout` for what each does. Extra arguments (`...`) are forwarded to
the underlying algorithm:

```{r}
#| label: layout-args

plot(dag, layout = "spring", seed = 1405, iterations = 500)
```

`layout` also accepts a pre-computed `data.frame` of `name`/`x`/`y` coordinates,
useful when comparing different graphs over the same nodes:

```{r}
#| label: layout-fixed

fixed <- data.frame(
  name = c("C", "A", "X", "K", "F", "D", "Y", "G", "H"),
  x = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4),
  y = c(1, -1, 0, -2, 1, -1, 0, -2, 0)
)
plot(dag, layout = fixed)
```

Notice also how the edge from $K$ to $Y$ automatically routed!

You can also call `cgraph_layout()` on your graph to get the positions, and
manually tweak a few nodes:

```{r}
#| label: layout-tweak

positions <- cgraph_layout(dag, method = "spring")
positions[positions$name == "A", c("x", "y")] <- c(0, 2)
plot(dag, layout = positions)
```

## Node styling

`node_style` accepts anything `grid::gpar()` understands (`fill`, `col`, `lwd`,
`lty`, `alpha`) plus geometry options: `padding` (mm, default 2, text clearance
kept when sizing to the label), `size` (multiplier on the computed node radius,
default 1), `radius` (mm; when set, every node is drawn at this fixed
half-extent instead of being fitted to its label), `shape`
(`"circle"`/`"square"`/`"ellipse"`/`"rect"`), and `linestyle` (e.g. `"dashed"`
for a non-solid border). `by_node` overrides any of these per node.

```{r}
#| label: node-style

plot(
  dag,
  node_style = list(
    fill = "lightblue",
    col = "navy",
    by_node = list(
      A = list(fill = "salmon", col = "firebrick"),
      Y = list(fill = "gold")
    )
  )
)
```

### Node shapes

`shape` is one of `"circle"` (the default), `"square"`, `"ellipse"`, or
`"rect"`. `"circle"`/`"square"` fit the label and always round out to equal
sides; `"ellipse"`/`"rect"` keep the fitted oblong box as-is - useful for
fitting a long label.

```{r}
#| label: node-shape

plot(
  dag,
  node_style = list(
    by_node = list(
      A = list(shape = "circle"),
      X = list(shape = "square"),
      Y = list(shape = "ellipse"),
      D = list(shape = "rect")
    )
  ),
  labels = c(A = "Confounder", X = "Exposure", Y = "Outcome", D = "Mediator")
)
```

`linestyle` styles the border:

```{r}
#| label: node-linestyle

plot(
  cgraph("U --> X + Y, X --> Y", class = "DAG"),
  node_style = list(
    col = "black",
    by_node = list(
      U = list(linestyle = "dashed", col = "gray50")
    )
  )
)
```

### Text-fit node sizing

By default each node is sized to fit its own label:

```{r}
#| label: text-fit

longlabels <- cgraph(
  "Exposure --> Mediator --> Y_outcome",
  class = "DAG"
)
plot(longlabels)
```

Pass `radius` explicitly to size every node uniformly instead:

```{r}
#| label: fixed-radius

plot(dag, node_style = list(radius = 8))
```

## Edge styling

`edge_style` accepts `grid::gpar()` fields (`col`, `lwd`, `lty`, `alpha`,
`fill`) plus `arrow_size` (mm, default 3), `circle_size` (mm, default 1.5, for
`o->`/`o--`/`o-o` endpoints), and `curvature` (unset by default; bows an edge
into an arc by this signed fraction of its length - positive bows left of the
`from`-to-`to` direction, negative right).

`fill` is the arrowhead's fill color and defaults to the edge's own `col`, so
arrowheads render solid by default. Pass `fill = NA` for the classic
hollow/outline arrowhead:

```{r}
#| label: edge-fill

plot(
  dag,
  edge_style = list(
    col = "darkgreen",
    fill = NA,
    lwd = 1.5
  )
)
```

### Per-type styling

`edge_style` can carry `directed`, `undirected`, `bidirected`,
`partially_directed` (`o->`), `partially_undirected` (`o--`), and `partial`
(`o-o`) sub-lists, so each of the six edge-mark groups can be styled
independently:

```{r}
#| label: edge-per-type

admg <- cgraph("X --> Y, X <-> Z, Z --> Y", class = "ADMG")
plot(
  admg,
  edge_style = list(
    directed = list(col = "steelblue"),
    bidirected = list(col = "firebrick", lwd = 2.5)
  )
)
```

### Per-edge overrides

`by_edge` is a named list keyed by node name. A node-wide entry (a plain style
list) applies to every edge touching that node; a pair-level entry
(`by_edge[[from]][[to]]`) targets every edge between that pair.

```{r}
#| label: edge-by-edge

plot(
  dag,
  edge_style = list(
    col = "gray50",
    by_edge = list(
      # Node-wide: every edge touching X...
      X = list(col = "steelblue"),
      # ...except X -> D specifically
      D = list(X = list(col = "red", lwd = 3))
    )
  )
)
```

Style precedence, highest to lowest: exact-edge-type override (`.by_type`,
below) > specific pair override in `by_edge` > node-wide override in `by_edge` >
per-type style > global style.

A pair-level `by_edge` entry can't tell apart parallel edges of different types
between the same pair (e.g. an `ADMG`'s `X --> Y` and `X <-> Y`). Nest one level
deeper under the reserved key `.by_type`, keyed by the edge's notation (`"-->"`,
`"<->"`, ...), to style one exact edge:

```{r}
#| label: edge-by-type

shared <- cgraph("X --> Y, X <-> Y", class = "ADMG")
plot(
  shared,
  edge_style = list(
    col = "steelblue",
    by_edge = list(
      X = list(
        Y = list(
          .by_type = list("-->" = list(col = "firebrick"))
        )
      )
    )
  )
)
```

Note that `X --> Y` and `X <-> Y` are automatically bent into two parallel arcs
rather than drawn on top of each other.

### Curved edges

`curvature` bows an edge into an arc instead of drawing it straight:

```{r}
#| label: curvature

plot(admg, edge_style = list(bidirected = list(curvature = -0.3)))
```

## Label styling

`label_style` sets the node-label text appearance: `col`, `fontsize`,
`fontface`, `fontfamily`, `cex`.

By default each node is labelled with its own name. `labels` overrides this,
falling back to a node's own name (or a `"default"` entry) when not mentioned;
node sizing accounts for multi-line labels (`\n`), so nodes grow to fit.

```{r}
#| label: labels

plot(
  cgraph("A0 --> L1 --> A1 --> Y, A0 --> Y + A1", class = "DAG"),
  labels = c(
    A0 = "Treatment\nat baseline",
    L1 = "Confounder\nat time 1",
    A1 = "Treatment\nat time 1"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: label-style

plot(dag, label_style = list(fontsize = 14, col = "navy"))
```

## Title

Pass `main` to add a plot title (`NULL` by default, i.e. no title).
`title_style` (same fields as `label_style`) styles it, and `title_gap` (default
`grid::unit(1, "lines")`) controls the spacing between the title and the graph.

```{r}
#| label: title

plot(dag, main = "My DAG", title_style = list(fontsize = 18, col = "navy"))
```

## Figure size and margins

`outer_margin` (default `grid::unit(2, "mm")`) pads the whole plot, and `asp`
fixes the y/x aspect ratio of the plotted data - `NA` (default) fills the
available space, `asp = 1` makes one x-unit equal one y-unit. The figure size
itself is set the usual R way, e.g. via `grDevices::pdf(width =, height =)` or
an RStudio/Quarto chunk's `fig-width`/`fig-height`, since `plot()` draws with
grid graphics into whatever device is already open.

```{r}
#| label: asp

plot(dag, asp = 1, main = "asp = 1")
```

## Tiers

Pass `tiers` (via `...`) to arrange nodes into left-to-right columns instead of
using `layout` - a named list of node-name vectors (list order is tier order,
names become tier labels), a named numeric vector (one tier number per node), or
a `data.frame` with `name`/`tier` columns. `tier_style` controls the boxes drawn
behind each tier: `boxes` (default `TRUE`), `labels` (logical or character
vector; `TRUE` uses the tier names), `fill`, `col`, `lwd`, `padding` (mm),
`label_style`, and `by_tier` (per-tier overrides keyed by tier name or 1-based
index).

```{r}
#| label: tiers

plot(
  dag,
  tiers = list(
    exposure = "A",
    mediators = c("X", "K", "D"),
    outcome = c("Y", "H")
  ),
  tier_style = list(labels = TRUE)
)
```

## Global styling defaults

`node_style`, `edge_style`, `label_style`, `title_style`, and `tier_style` each
default to the corresponding entry from `plot_options()` (itself defaulting to
`plot_default_options()`). Set them globally with `plot_options()` to avoid
repeating the same style lists at every call site - arguments passed to `plot()`
still take precedence:

```{r}
#| label: plot-options

plot_options(node_style = list(fill = "white", col = "black"))
plot(dag)

# Reset to the built-in defaults
plot_options(plot_default_options())
```

## Combining options

Here we plot a `PAG` where we combine a bunch of different styling options:

```{r}
#| label: combined

pag <- cgraph(
  "C o-> X, D --> G + Y, X --> D + F, Y --> H, K o-> X, K --> Y",
  class = "PAG"
)

plot(
  pag,
  node_style = list(
    fill = "#f8fafc",
    col = "#64748b",
    by_node = list(
      X = list(fill = "#dbeafe", col = "#2563eb"),
      Y = list(fill = "#fef3c7", col = "#d97706"),
      K = list(linestyle = "dashed")
    )
  ),
  edge_style = list(
    col = "#334155",
    partially_directed = list(col = "#2563eb")
  ),
  label_style = list(col = "#1e293b", fontsize = 16),
  main = "A PAG",
  title_style = list(fontsize = 18, col = "#1e293b")
)
```
